versions.text: Criterion: Verify that the software development process for Safety Supporting Software Elements (SSSEs) is fully documented (e.g., Software Development Plan (SDP), Software Safety Plan (SSP)), followed, and is sufficiently suitable to produce software supporting SCFs. Standard: Identify all SSSEs via a documented SCF thread analysis and flow down of system safety requirements. SSSEs adhere to a rigorous development process which is suitable, comprehensive, well defined, documented and consistently applied. The processes and activities are applied to all software intended for use (e.g., new development, commercial-off-the-shelf/government-off-the-shelf (COTS/GOTS), reuse, legacy, firmware). The processes and associated life cycle activities are based on a development standard that represents a high integrity process for safety critical software. The development process is documented in an SDP (or set of SDPs) that addresses all activities required for the developing organizations. The activities are identified to support the SSSE requirements, design, code, integration, test and release of products. The SDP may reference other documents and data as part of identifying all processes and related activities (e.g., coding standards, system safety plan, risk management plan, configuration management plan, and quality assurance plan). Development processes for SSSEs and non-SSSEs may be addressed in the same SDP. Method of Compliance: Verification method includes inspection of process and product documentation. Verify that the SSSEs are identified and documented. Verify that the SSSE development processes address the following areas and the defined processes are followed: a. Functional analysis (e.g., SCF thread analysis). b. SCF testing methodology. c. Quality Assurance. d. Configuration Management. e. Coding standards. f. System Safety. g. Peer reviews. h. Software test methodology (unit level, software integration, software requirements, etc.). i. Regression test methodology. j. Verification/qualification environment (e.g., system integration laboratory). k. FMET. l. Risk management. m. Software Review Board composition. n. Traceability. o. Manpower. p. Metrics. q. Software discrepancy reports. r. Change impact analysis. s. SSSE architecture support of SPA. t. Requirement definition and allocation. u. Software engineering environment. v. Software reuse. w. Areas of auto code. References: JSSG-2008 Appendix A: 3.1.14.6, 3.2.4.6, 3.3.6 and 3.3.7 including various subparagraphs of each provide guidance regarding software design and development for safety critical systems DoD JSSSEH USAF Weapon Systems Software Management Guidebook RTCA DO-178: (see also DO-178B) SAE 12207.1-1997: 6.17 software development process IEEE Std 1228-1994 Software Safety Plans FAA AC 20-115C

Standard: 1. Verify that the software development process for SESSs is fully documented (e.g., SDP, Software Safety Plan), followed, and is sufficiently suitable to produce software supporting SCFs. Identify all SESSs via a documented SCFTA. SESSs adhere to a rigorous development process which is suitable, comprehensive, well defined, documented, and consistently applied. The processes and activities are applied to all software intended for use (e.g., new development, COTS, GOTS, reuse, legacy). The processes and associated life cycle activities are based on a development standard that represents a high integrity process for safety-critical software. The development process is documented in an SDP (or set of SDPs) that addresses all activities required for the developing organizations. The activities are identified to support the SESS requirements, design, code, integration, verification, validation, and release of products. The SDP may reference other documents and data as part of identifying all processes and related activities (e.g., coding standards, system safety plan, risk management plan, CM plan, and quality assurance plan). Development processes for SESSs and SENSSs may be addressed in the same SDP. The software development processes account for developing SESS software to operate with the technologies utilized (e.g., MCPs). Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): The number next to an MoC line item corresponds to the numbered line item in the standard that is being verified: 1. Verification method includes examination of process and product documentation. Verify that the SESSs are identified and documented. Verify that the SESS development processes address the following areas and the defined processes are followed: a. Functional analysis (e.g., SCFTA). b. Safety-critical function testing methodology. c. Quality assurance. d. Configuration management. e. Coding standards. f. System safety. g. Peer reviews. h. Software test methodology (e.g., unit-level, software integration, software requirements). i. Regression test methodology. j. Verification environment (e.g., SIL). k. Failure modes and effects testing. l. Risk management. m. Software Review Board composition. n. Traceability. o. Metrics relevant to data used to support AW criteria (e.g., throughput utilization, structural coverage, requirement verification coverage). p. Software discrepancy reports. q. Change impact analysis. r. SESS architecture support of SPA. s. Requirement definition and allocation. t. Software engineering environment. u. Software reuse. v. Areas of auto code. w. Processes adequately account for the technologies utilized (e.g., MCPs).
